slides.title: LumiTac: Compact, High-Rate Six-Axis Optical Tactile Sensing for Human-Robot Interaction
slides.highlight: This work introduces LumiTac, a compact, low-cost optical tactile sensor capable of high-rate six-axis force and moment reconstruction, validated for tactile-guided manipulation and physical human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: LumiTac is a compact, low-cost optical tactile sensor enabling high-rate six-axis force and moment measurement for robotics.
card.key_idea: Uses spatially distributed RGBW emitters/receivers across silicone layers; an MLP reconstructs six-axis loads from 20 optical channels.
card.evaluation: Validated via reference F/T sensor (R²>0.96, MAE<0.2N); demonstrated 303Hz update rate in combined loading and robot control tasks.
card.limitation: Accuracy relies on silicone stability and optical alignment; ambient light and elastomer nonlinearity remain calibration challenges.

slides.title: Which Physical Tactile Cues Matter for Contact-Rich Imitation Learning? A Controlled Real-Robot Study
slides.tldr: TACTILE CUE ANALYSIS FOR IMITATION LEARNING
slides.highlight: This study isolates the impact of specific physical tactile cues on imitation learning, revealing that marker flow is the most effective individual signal and that cue-factorized encoding significantly boosts performance.

card.one_liner: Marker flow is the most effective tactile cue for contact-rich imitation learning, significantly boosting success rates.
card.key_idea: Compares tactile RGB, depth, and marker flow cues in real-robot imitation learning to identify which physical signals drive policy performance.
card.evaluation: 720 real-robot trials on LeRobot; tactile cues improved success from 57.8% to 78.9%, with marker flow yielding 74.4%.
card.limitation: Tactile fusion effectiveness is task-dependent, and results rely on specific sensor hardware and policy backbones.

slides.title: Correct Robots Before They Make Mistakes: Proactive Human-in-the-Loop Intervention via Preference Learning
slides.tldr: PROACTIVE HUMAN INTERVENTION VIA PREFERENCE LEARNING
slides.highlight: The PHIL framework enables proactive human-in-the-loop correction by allowing operators to intervene on predicted robot trajectories before errors occur, using preference learning to improve policy success rates. This approach aligns with MOSAIC's goal of enhancing human-AI coadaptation through iterative feedback and skill acquisition.

card.one_liner: PHIL uses XR previews for proactive human corrections, boosting robot success via preference-based post-training.
card.key_idea: Operators preview predicted trajectories in XR to intervene before errors; rejected predictions are paired with corrective actions for preference learning.
card.evaluation: Tested on four real-world tasks with diffusion and VLA policies; outperformed HG-DAgger (44% to 70% success) using five correction episodes.
card.limitation: Requires specialized XR hardware and skilled operators to accurately anticipate errors and provide timely interventions.

slides.title: PanoTac: A Dense Three-Axis Tactile Sensor for Robust Touch-Centric Manipulation
slides.highlight: PanoTac offers a low-cost, compliant tactile fingertip providing dense three-axis sensing, significantly improving contact-rich manipulation tasks like grain scooping over vision-only baselines.

card.one_liner: PanoTac is a low-cost, dense three-axis tactile fingertip that significantly improves touch-centric robotic manipulation.
card.key_idea: Combines piezoresistive arrays for contact geometry with magnetic sensors for shear, yielding a 12x32x3 tactile representation.
card.evaluation: Tested on three manipulation tasks; outperformed vision-only baselines by 46.7% on average, with ablations confirming both modalities' importance.
card.limitation: Susceptible to external magnetic interference, limited force resolution, and currently designed only for parallel-jaw grippers.

slides.title: Exploring Proximity and Tactile Sensing for Robotic Manipulation
slides.highlight: This work introduces a multimodal tactile sensor combining time-of-flight and pressure sensing to enable anticipatory robotic manipulation, relevant to HyECHO's interest in non-data-hungry multimodal perception of physical interactions.

card.one_liner: ToFTouch integrates multizone time-of-flight and tactile sensing to enable anticipatory robotic manipulation in cluttered environments.
card.key_idea: Combines three 4x4 multizone ToF proximity sensors with an optics-based tactile array on a compact gripper-mounted module for pre-contact and contact feedback.
card.evaluation: Tested on pre-grasp, extraction, and insertion tasks using a Franka robot; showed 7.4% cycle time reduction and robust depth correction against baselines.
card.limitation: Results rely on limited trials; sensor overheating causes data corruption, and lack of calibration leads to depth measurement discrepancies.

slides.title: Dexterous Robotic Hands in the Foundation-Model Era: A Full-Stack Survey
slides.tldr: SURVEY OF DEXTEROUS HANDS AND FOUNDATION MODELS
slides.highlight: This survey synthesizes recent advances in dexterous robotic hands, highlighting that human data value depends on kinematic and contact alignment rather than volume, and that foundation models do not eliminate embodiment-specific physical constraints.

card.one_liner: A full-stack survey of dexterous robotic hands, covering hardware, data, transfer, learning, and evaluation.
card.key_idea: Organizes literature into five interdependent layers (hardware, data, transfer, learning, evaluation) to analyze how design choices propagate across the stack.
card.evaluation: Structured narrative review of 2024-2026 sources, including comparative tables, case studies, and quantitative synthesis of reported evidence.
card.limitation: Not an exhaustive systematic review; lacks independent dual-review records and may suffer from publication and positive-result biases.

slides.title: Learning Object-Centric Motion Priors from Human for Robotic Dexterous Manipulation
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates how leveraging Human-Object Interaction datasets to predict future hand-object states can serve as general-purpose rewards for reinforcement learning, enhancing dexterous manipulation generalization. This aligns with RwB's focus on embodied learning and improving human-robot interaction through data-driven priors.

card.one_liner: Learns object-centric motion priors from human data to guide RL for generalizable dexterous manipulation.
card.key_idea: Predicts future hand-object states via a transformer on HOI data; uses predicted object poses as a general reward for RL.
card.evaluation: Tested on YCB grasping, articulated objects, and obstacles in sim and real robots; outperforms SOTA baselines in success rates.
card.limitation: Relies on accurate 6DoF object pose estimation and may struggle with objects lacking clear HOI dataset priors.

slides.title: ForceLDM: A Force-aware Latent Dynamics Model for Contact-Rich Manipulation
slides.highlight: This work introduces a latent dynamics model that distills future force and motion signals into a compact representation, enabling robust contact-rich manipulation without relying on future sensory inputs at deployment. It is relevant to MOSAIC as it addresses the challenge of modeling physical interaction dynamics and force-based states, which are critical for estimating procedural skill and aligning human-AI intent in tasks like wire-harness assembly.

card.one_liner: ForceLDM distills future force and motion dynamics into a student policy for robust contact-rich manipulation.
card.key_idea: Teacher-student distillation aligns student queries with teacher representations of future force/torque and optical flow, avoiding pixel-space prediction.
card.evaluation: Five real-world tasks (USB, VGA, etc.) vs. π0, TA-VLA, ForceVLA; 87.1% ID and 68.9% OOD success rates.
card.limitation: Relies on small datasets; 2D optical flow lacks depth and suffers from occlusion or motion blur errors.
